article_content: BAGHDAD, Iraq (CNN) — Over 1,000 Iraqi detainees released in recent weeks under Operation Lion's Paw have not violated their pledge to abstain from insurgency, according to Maj. Gen. Doug Stone, the U.S. Marine general overseeing detention centers in Iraq. Speaking in Arabic on Wednesday, Stone emphasized efforts to rehabilitate the 25,000 detainees—predominantly Sunnis—through education, vocational training, and inter-sectarian cooperation. Detainees receive medical care equivalent to U.S. military personnel, halal food, and family visitation rights. The program aims to break cycles of violence and poverty, with 8,000 detainees enrolled in schooling (including 7,000 who passed fifth-grade exams) and all 860 minors required to attend classes. Despite these measures, Sunni political groups like the Iraqi Accord Front cite detention policies as a key reason for withdrawing from the government earlier this year. Stone noted that releases will continue post-Ramadan, contrasting current practices with the shuttered Abu Ghraib facility, which was demolished following abuse scandals. 'Our facilities are transparent and open to credible inspections,' he stated.
translated_content: BAGHDAD, Iraq (CNN) — Mahigit 1,000 detaineedong Iraqi na pinalaya kamakailan sa ilalim ng Operation Lion's Paw ay hindi sumuway sa kanilang pangakong tumigil sa pag-alsa, ayon kay Maj. Gen. Doug Stone ng U.S. Marines na namamahala sa mga detention center sa Iraq. Sa pahayag na ibinahagi sa Arabe noong Miyerkules, binigyang-diin ni Stone ang rehabilitasyon ng 25,000 detainee—pangunahing mga Sunni—sa pamamagitan ng edukasyon, pagsasanay sa trabaho, at pagtutulungan ng iba't ibang sektor. Tumanggap ang mga detainee ng medical care na kapareho ng mga sundalong Amerikano, halal na pagkain, at karapatang makabisita sa pamilya. Layunin ng programa na puksain ang siklo ng karahasan at kahirapan, kung saan 8,000 detainee ang nakapag-aral (kasama ang 7,000 na pumasa sa ika-5 baitang) at lahat ng 860 menor de edad ay sapilitang pumasok sa klase. Sa kabila nito, itinuro ng mga grupong Sunni tulad ng Iraqi Accord Front ang patakaran sa detention bilang dahilan ng pag-alis nila sa gobyerno noong nakaraang taon. Giit ni Stone, magpapatuloy ang pagpapalaya pagkatapos ng Ramadan, na kaiba sa dating pasilidad ng Abu Ghraib na winasak matapos ang iskandalong pagmamalupit. 'Bukas sa inspeksyon ang aming mga detention center,' pagdidiin niya.

article_content: Two men received prison sentences this week for a brutal assault on a visually impaired young man and his father in Hull. Michael Chaplin, 21, was sentenced to five years, while 19-year-old Darrell Hughes received three years for the June attack that left both victims with severe injuries. The court heard how the violence erupted when the 21-year-old victim, who is registered blind, greeted the pair with 'alright lads' while returning home with his father after watching a football match. Hughes reportedly spat at the young man before both attackers began punching him. As the father tried to intervene, Hughes chased him down and struck him repeatedly with a 'for sale' sign. Chaplin escalated the attack by using a brick to strike the blind victim's face three times, causing multiple fractures. Both assailants then kicked the father over 20 times before stealing his shoes. The traumatized son fled the scene, later telling police: 'I genuinely thought they'd killed my dad. I ran home in complete darkness, terrified they'd catch me.' Judge Jeremy Richardson described the assault as 'particularly appalling' given the victim's disability, noting the attackers showed 'no mercy.' Medical reports confirmed the father suffered facial swelling and eye injuries, while the son required treatment for serious facial fractures. Court records revealed both attackers had prior violent offenses. Chaplin had a 2008 conviction for assault, while Hughes had previously attacked his own parents.
translated_content: Dalawang lalaki, nahatulan ng pagkakakulong dahil sa malupit na pag-atake sa isang bulag na binata at sa kanyang ama sa Hull. Si Michael Chaplin (21 anyos), limang taong sentensiya; si Darrell Hughes (19 anyos), tatlong taon sa pangyayaring Hunyo na nagdulot ng malubha ring pinsala sa mga biktima. Ayon sa korte, nagsimula ang karahasan nang batiin ng bulag na binata ang dalawa ng 'Kamusta mga pare' habang pauwi kasama ang ama pagkatapos manood ng laban sa football. Unang lumura si Hughes sa biktima bago magsimula ang pagpapalo. Nang sumaklolo ang ama, hinabol siya ni Hughes at pinalo nang paulit-ulit gamit ang karatula ng 'for sale'. Pinalala ni Chaplin ang pag-atake gamit ang isang ladrilyo, tinamaan ang mukha ng biktima nang tatlong beses na nagresulta sa bali. Parehong sinipa ang ama nang mahigit 20 beses at kinuha ang kanyang sapatos. Gulong-gulo ang binata: 'Naniwala akong pinatay na nila ang tatay ko. Tumakbo ako sa kadiliman, nangangatog sa takot.' Binigyang-diin ni Hukom Jeremy Richardson ang 'nakakagigil na pangyayari', lalo't may kapansanan ang biktima. Parehong may naunang kaso ng pananakit ang mga akusado.
post_content: Shocking hate crime in Hull: Two men jailed for brutal attack on blind man & father. Perps used bricks & signs in unprovoked assault. Judge slams 'no mercy' shown. #JusticeForDisabled #EndStreetViolence
translated_post: Malupit na pag-atake sa bulag na binata at ama sa Hull! Dalawang lalaki, nakakulong na. Ginamit pa ang ladrilyo't karatula sa pananakit. Hukom: 'Walang awa ang ginawa.' #KatarunganParaSaMayKapansanan #LabananAngKarahanasan

article_content: By Daniel Martin | Published: 14 June 2013  Prime Minister David Cameron has acknowledged working in his pajamas during early mornings before changing into formal attire. This admission came during a BBC World Have Your Say program where he responded to a Turkish viewer's question about balancing work and life at 10 Downing Street.  The Prime Minister stated: 'I rise very early and begin work before dressing formally. The short answer is yes, I do sometimes work in sleepwear.' This disclosure highlights Cameron's informal style while addressing past criticisms about his work hours.  While known for leisure activities like playing the Fruit Ninja mobile game and weekly tennis matches, Cameron maintains he works 'incredibly hard.' The Spectator magazine previously reported his extensive iPad gaming habits.
